summary: Redwood hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming responses, tuning parameters (temperature, max_tokens, top_p), retries/backoff, and common enterprise concerns (SOC2, KMS, data retention). Horizon is evaluating for a customer-facing chat assistant and internal summarization pipelines; interest in latency SLOs and predictable cost. Agreed to run a POC/benchmark to validate streaming + retry semantics and to share security/compliance docs.
topics: Streaming responses and when to use chunked vs full payload
Generation params: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences
Retry behavior, idempotency, and exponential backoff
Rate limiting and quotas; cost-per-token tradeoffs
Hosted vs Dedicated for predictable latency and isolation
SOC2, KMS integration, and data residency questions
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan Park from Redwood, with Maya who'll run the deeper demo. Liam, Priya, Samir, thanks for making time. Is the time good?
[00:12] Liam: Yep, good here. We just have an hour blocked but 45 is fine. Quick context  Horizon is building a customer chat assistant plus doc summarization for ops. Main concerns: latency and costs.
[00:28] Maya: Great, we'll focus on chat/text generation basics and show streaming, param tuning, and our retry semantics. Small heads up  transcript might mangle some names, apologies.
[00:42] Priya: Perfect. We want to understand how streaming works for partial tokens, and how retries affect message ordering. Also curious about prefix cache, is that the K V cache you mentioned?
[00:58] Maya: Yes, KV cache  sometimes shows in logs as K V cache, the runtime keeps kv state across tokens to avoid re-compute. For streaming we send delta chunks over websocket or HTTP chunked and clients can render partial responses.
[01:18] Samir: Any gotchas for mobile clients with flaky networks? Retries could duplicate tokens, right?
[01:30] Ethan: Right, so two parts: client-level idempotency + server retry. We recommend an idempotency key on the conversation turn; if retry happens within the server window we dedupe. Also we expose a streaming cursor so the client can resume.
[01:46] Liam: Can you demo a basic streaming chat call?
[01:52] Maya: Sure  switching to the console. (background: mouse clicks) We'll run a sample conversation. Note: this is using our hosted API model redwood-chat-medium, a curated open-model variant.
[02:10] Maya: [typing] First call with temp=0.2 and max_tokens=150. Starting stream...
[02:25] Speaker 1: "Hello, how can I help you today?" (streamed chunk)
[02:40] Priya: Nice, the first token arrived in about 90ms on this demo infra  your real latency will vary by region and model.
[02:55] Maya: Now I'll show a higher temperature 0.9 for more creative responses. Notice the chunk pattern is similar, but variance in token content.
[03:14] Liam: On pricing  is streaming charged differently? Do you charge on tokens generated only or also on tokens streamed?
[03:27] Ethan: It's per-token generated; streaming doesn't incur extra unit charges beyond tokens. We do also show per-token latency and cost breakdowns in Console.
[03:45] Samir: Regarding params  top_p vs temperature guidance?
[03:52] Maya: Short answer: temperature controls randomness globally, top_p is nucleus sampling. For deterministic behavior stick to temp 0-0.2 and lower top_p. We also recommend stop sequences to avoid run-on outputs for chat.
[04:10] Priya: If we set stop sequences, how does streaming behave when stop is met mid-chunk?
[04:20] Maya: Stream truncates as soon as the model emits stop tokens; we flush the final chunk. There can be a tiny final chunk with closing punctuation.
[04:35] Liam: Retries  what does the default retry/backoff look like?
[04:42] Ethan: For transient 5xx errors we recommend exponential backoff with jitter; Redwood SDKs have built-in retry helpers. For streaming we prefer reconnect+resume with last-token cursor to avoid full re-generation.
[05:00] Priya: Do you guarantee at-most-once semantics?
[05:07] Maya: We aim for at-most-once within the request window if you provide an idempotency key; otherwise duplicates are possible on retries.
[05:20] Samir: How about rate limiting  per-account and per-route?
[05:26] Ethan: Both. Hosted API has account-level quotas and per-route configs. You can request higher limits or move to Dedicated for guaranteed throughput.
[05:40] Liam: If we hit a spike during black friday-like traffic, what's the recommended pattern?
[05:47] Maya: For spikes, we recommend graceful degradation: lower max_tokens, increase batching at the client side for background tasks, or route higher volume to a cheaper quantized model. Smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants automatically.
[06:05] Priya: Can you show how to set those params in the REST call?
[06:10] Maya: Sure  example payload: {"model":"redwood-chat-medium","messages":[...],"temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":150,"top_p":0.9}. In the SDK it's a params object. (note: sample shows curly braces in the console)
[06:32] Liam: Are embeddings separate billing? We're also considering semantic search.
[06:37] Ethan: Yes embeddings are billed per embedding unit. Console shows combined usage views so you can see chat vs embed spend.
[06:48] Priya: Security  SOC2 and KMS. We need BYOK and customer-managed keys for the PII flows.
[06:56] Maya: We support KMS/HSM integration in Hosted (enterprise tier) and Private deployments. We'll share the SOC2 report and KMS integration guide after the call.
[07:10] Samir: Data residency? Some EU customers require data stay in region.
[07:15] Ethan: You can pin region for hosting and we maintain audit logs. For strict residency we recommend Private VPC/on-prem option.
[07:28] Liam: Let's talk about latency targets  we want 300ms p95 for simple chat prompts. Possible?
[07:36] Maya: For small prompts with short context and CPU warm, 300ms p95 is achievable on dedicated GPU pools; hosted is often in the 400-600ms range depending on model and region. We can benchmark.
[07:50] Priya: For the POC can we run a scripted load to measure p50/p95 and cost per 10k messages?
[07:58] Maya: Yes, we'll run a POC with your sample prompts and measure tokens, latency, and error rates. We'll instrument KV cache hit rates too.
[08:12] Ethan: Quick question  how many end users and expected concurrency?
[08:18] Liam: Initial launch 50k monthly active users, peak concurrency ~200, mainly short utterances.
[08:27] Ethan: Good to know  that suggests hosted might be OK for pilot, but dedicated could be better for SLA and cost predictability at scale.
[08:38] Samir: Ok show us the retry logs in Console.
[08:44] Maya: Switching over  Console > Observability > Requests. Here you can filter for stream errors. You see retries annotated with idempotency key. There's also per-route token cost and latency histogram.
[09:05] Priya: The UI shows 'K V cache hits' as KV cache hits  sometimes the labels get spaced.
[09:12] Maya: Yeah small typo in some UI strings in the beta build. We'll note that.
[09:22] Liam: Any limits on streaming chunk size?
[09:26] Maya: We chunk at roughly token boundaries; chunk size is tunable but we recommend 200-500 bytes per chunk for stable streaming on mobile.
[09:36] Samir: How do you handle conversation state if we want to store it ourselves vs relying on Redwood?
[09:43] Ethan: You can store conversation turns client-side or in your DB. We support partial context via context IDs and allow passing custom context to model calls. There's also prefix caching to reduce cost if reusing the same context.
[09:58] Priya: For replays and audits, can we get full transcripts and token-level costs?
[10:03] Maya: Yes  Console exposes token-level cost per request and full transcript logs for the retention window tied to your plan. We'll share the retention table.
[10:16] Liam: About fallbacks  if a model is overloaded, can we automatically fallback to a smaller quantized model?
[10:23] Maya: Yes, smart routing policies allow fallback to predefined model variants; you can configure latency-first or cost-first policies.
[10:33] Ethan: Alright, quick recap before POC plan: we'll send pricing and quotas, SOC2/KMS docs, and propose the POC script. Any other blockers?
[10:44] Priya: Nightly batch summarization  how does batching affect embeddings vs streaming?
[10:51] Maya: Batch for offline jobs is best  fewer startup costs. For real-time streaming you can't batch much, so you tune model size and cache. For summaries we recommend condensed prompts and using a summarization-optimized model.
[11:07] Liam: Can you email a sample SDK snippet for reconnect+resume logic?
[11:12] Ethan: Yes, will attach in the follow-up.
[11:20] Samir: Anything about legal/contracting  we may need a data processing addendum.
[11:26] Ethan: We have an addendum template; legal can start review once you accept the pilot terms.
[11:34] Priya: One more question  do you support function calling / tool invocation?
[11:40] Maya: Yes, we support structured outputs and function-like tool calls. It can be streamed as JSON chunks and we can validate schema on the fly.
[11:52] Liam: Solid. Let's schedule the POC on 2026-04-12 as discussed.
[11:57] Ethan: Great, I'll send invites and next steps. Thanks everyone.
[12:02] (call ends)

Note: transcription contains occasional spacing issues for acronyms (e.g., K V cache). References: console screenshots and sample SDK snippets will be attached to follow-up email: https://redwood.example.com/docs/hosted-api and SOC2/KMS doc link placeholder.
